title: Tanzanian Chapati Roll
community: Urban Tanzania — the portable lunch roll
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Chapati Roll — a warm chapati filled with spiced beef or chicken, kachumbari, pili pili sauce, and coriander, rolled up and served immediately. The portable Tanzanian lunch — everything in one hand.
longDesc: The chapati roll is the Tanzanian answer to the burrito — a warm chapati loaded with spiced meat, fresh salad, and sauce, rolled up and eaten on the move. It is sold at every bus station, office district, and market.
ingredients: 150g spiced minced beef or chicken — warm
steps: Warm chapatis briefly in a dry pan.
Lay flat. Spread mayonnaise across the centre.
Add warm spiced meat along the centre.
Top with kachumbari, chilli, and coriander.
Fold in the sides. Roll up tightly.
chefTips: The chapati must be warm — cold chapati tears and does not roll.
Do not overfill — rolling becomes messy.
The pili pili goes in based on the customer's preference.
cookingScience: A warm chapati is more plastic (flexible) than a cold one — gluten strands remain relaxed and extensible at higher temperatures, allowing the chapati to roll without cracking. Below approximately 40°C, the starch granules re-crystallise and the chapati becomes brittle.
sustainabilityTips: Minimal packaging — the paper wrap is the only waste.
healthBenefits: Complete meal — protein, carbohydrate, and vegetables.
culturalNote: The chapati roll is Dar es Salaam's office lunch — fast, portable, and satisfying. It has become the unofficial street food of Tanzania's urban working class, eaten standing at the vendor's counter or walking back to the office.
